observations:
All conceptual domains in Torah #135 are accounted for by the two proposed packages and can be accommodated within them. No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was identified that is structurally separate from the existing two packages.

The two gap concepts identified in torah_135_additions.json (יוֹם-טוֹב as a bechina of בינה/מוחין דאמא, and יְמֵי דִּין as a bechina of יראה/מלכות) both extend Package 1 (מלכות וענוה) rather than forming an independent thematic family. They are additional nodes that deepen Package 1's domain.

The Torah's argument follows a two-stage structure:
  Stage 1 — The tzaddik/Yom Tov as the great light that annuls arrogance [Package 2: good]
  Stage 2 — The domain of holy malkhut/humility/yirah that is revealed by that annulment [Package 1: good]

The teaching is entirely positive in its bechina structure: it describes the good/holy pole (tzaddik = Yom Tov holiness) and the human inner dimension that this reveals (malkhut/humility/fear). The evil counterpart — the four kingdoms of the sitra achra, the kingdom of Amalek — is present in the source text as the target of Yom Tov's action (narrative/eitza), but does not generate standalone bechina-connected nodes for this Torah in the dataset.

Good/evil mirror: The implicit evil mirror of Package 1 (מלכות דקדושה/יראה) is מַלְכוּת עֲמָלֵק / אַרְבַּע מַלְכֻיּוֹת דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא — same structure (a kingdom that draws its power from human worship), opposite orientation (it draws from the absence of yirat Elohim, i.e., the absence of malkhut dikdusha). Line 27 states this explicitly: 'עִקַּר כֹּחוֹ [של עמלק] הָיָה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלוּ אֶת הַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם יִרְאַת אֱלֹקִים.' The evil mirror is structurally present in the Torah's argument but does not manifest as a separate bechina-package in the current data — it surfaces only in eitza context. No new evil package is proposed based on the available bechina edges.

Torah #135 is structurally one of the simpler Torahs in the corpus: compact, focused on a single teaching axis (Yom Tov/Tzaddik → annulment of arrogance → holy malkhut/humility), with only 7 bechina edges total and 10 nodes.
